title.en: Volume 379 Biographies 166: Zhao Shenzhen, Lu Kun, Ceng Sheng, Tao Shu
title.raw: 卷379 列傳一百六十六 赵慎畛 卢坤 曾胜 陶澍

sentences.zh: 列傳一百六十六

translations.literal: Biographies 166
translations.idiomatic: Biography 166

sentences.zh: 趙慎畛盧坤曾勝陶澍

translations.literal: Zhao Shenzhen, Lu Kun, Ceng Sheng, Tao Shu
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shenzhen, Lu Kun, Ceng Sheng, and Tao Shu

sentences.zh: 趙慎畛，字笛樓，湖南武陵人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shenzhen, styled Dilou, was a man of Wuling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shenzhen, whose courtesy name was Dilou, came from Wuling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 為諸生時，學政錢灃器之，曰：「人英也！

translations.literal: When he was a licentiate, the educational commissioner Qian Feng valued him, saying: "He is a paragon among men!
translations.idiomatic: While still a licentiate student, the educational commissioner Qian Feng took him in high regard and said, "Here is a paragon among men!

sentences.zh: 」嘉慶元年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of the Jiaqing reign he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and then to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 條上川、楚善後屯田保甲事宜。

translations.literal: He submitted in detail post-pacification garrison-farming and baojia matters for Sichuan and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out in detail proposals on garrison farming and the baojia system for the post-rebellion administration of Sichuan and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 巡通州漕，革陋規，廉得楊村通判科索剝船，奏褫其職。

translations.literal: Inspecting grain transport at Tongzhou, he abolished corrupt practices; upon investigation he found the assistant prefect at Yangcun extorting and stripping transport boats, and memorialized to strip him of office.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting grain transport at Tongzhou he abolished entrenched abuses, uncovered the Yangcun assistant prefect's extortion and stripping of transport boats, and memorialized for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 湖南學政徐松矜愎失士心，欲附慎畛自固，常列其弟子優等，慎畛列款糾劾罷之。

translations.literal: The Hunan educational commissioner Xu Song was arrogant and had lost scholars' hearts; wishing to attach himself to Shenzhen for security, he often ranked Shenzhen's students in the top grade. Shenzhen listed particulars in a memorial of impeachment and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan educational commissioner Xu Song was arrogant and had lost the regard of the scholarly community; hoping to secure himself by currying favor with Shenzhen, he habitually ranked Shenzhen's pupils in the top grade. Shenzhen set out the facts in a memorial of impeachment and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 兩廣總督蔣攸銛薦其才可大用。

translations.literal: The governor-general of the Two Guangs, Jiang Youxian, recommended that his talent could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian, governor-general of Liangguang, recommended him as a man whose ability warranted high appointment.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出為廣東惠潮嘉道。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In his seventeenth year of service he was posted as intendant of the Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嚴治械鬥，捕南澳、澄海、潮陽盜甚眾；

translations.literal: He strictly governed armed affrays and captured very many bandits at Nan'ao, Chenghai, and Chaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down hard on armed clan fights and captured large numbers of bandits at Nan'ao, Chenghai, and Chaoyang;

sentences.zh: 沿海民寮居為逋逃藪，悉編入保甲。

translations.literal: coastal Miao and Yao inhabitants lived in places that became refuges for fugitives; he had them all registered in baojia.
translations.idiomatic: along the coast, Miao and Yao communities had become havens for fugitives, and he registered them all under the baojia system.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to provincial judge of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to provincial judge of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 天地會匪結黨構亂，脅有貲者入其中，慎畛惟嚴罪匪首，被脅者不坐。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth Society bandits formed cliques and plotted rebellion, coercing the wealthy to join; Shenzhen imposed severe punishment only on ringleaders, and those coerced were not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth Society bandits formed factions and plotted rebellion, forcing wealthy men to join them; Shenzhen punished only the ringleaders severely, and those who had been coerced were not charged.

sentences.zh: 廣東洋匪投誠後，漸入廣西為盜。

translations.literal: After Guangdong coastal pirates had submitted, they gradually entered Guangxi and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After coastal pirates in Guangdong had surrendered, they gradually crossed into Guangxi and turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 設水路巡船以護商旅，督守令以捕盜多少為殿最。

translations.literal: He established waterway patrol boats to protect merchants and travelers, and supervised prefects and magistrates, ranking them by how many bandits they captured.
translations.idiomatic: He set up patrol boats on the waterways to protect merchants and travelers, and ranked prefects and magistrates by the number of bandits they captured for rewards and penalties.

sentences.zh: 遠郡招解重囚煩費，吏因諱盜，省文法，嚴舉劾，緝捕始力。

translations.literal: In distant prefectures escorting serious criminals was costly and troublesome; officials therefore concealed banditry. He reduced legal formalities, imposed strict impeachment, and only then did pursuit and capture become effective.
translations.idiomatic: In remote prefectures the cost of escorting serious criminals was so burdensome that officials concealed crimes; he streamlined legal formalities, enforced strict impeachment, and only then did pursuit and arrest become effective.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷廣東布政使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 州縣多積虧，展轉相承，悉心鉤稽，除其糾轕，庫儲頓增。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties had many accumulated deficits passed from hand to hand; he painstakingly audited accounts, cleared entanglements, and treasury reserves suddenly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties carried heavy deficits passed from one term to the next; he painstakingly audited the books, untangled the accounts, and treasury reserves rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 南海、高要瀕河堤防多圮，民苦水患，籌款生息資歲修，屯田五千餘頃。

translations.literal: At Nanhai and Gaoyao the river dikes were largely breached and the people suffered from floods; he raised funds to earn interest for annual repairs and had more than five thousand qing of garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: River dikes at Nanhai and Gaoyao along the Pearl River were largely in ruins and the people suffered chronic flooding; he raised capital to generate interest for annual repairs and reclaimed more than five thousand qing of garrison land.

sentences.zh: 賦重為累，請減糧額，攤抵於沙坦輕則之地。

translations.literal: Heavy taxation was a burden; he requested reduction of grain quotas, apportioned onto lightly taxed sandy flats.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy tax quotas were crushing the people; he petitioned to reduce grain assessments and spread the burden onto lightly taxed sandy flats.

sentences.zh: 粵俗奢靡，刊發陳宏謀行政訓俗遺規，躬行節儉以示勸。

translations.literal: Cantonese customs were extravagant; he published Chen Hongmou's Administrative Regulations for Custom Reform and personally practiced frugality to encourage others.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese customs were notoriously extravagant; he published Chen Hongmou's surviving regulations on administration and moral instruction, and himself practiced frugality to set an example.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 習知粵西地勢如建瓴，旬日不雨即旱竭，勸民修隄塘，造龍骨車，開廕井，設井筒架，皆頒式俾仿行。

translations.literal: Knowing well that western Guangdong's terrain was like water held in a tilted jar—ten days without rain and drought would set in—he urged the people to repair dikes and ponds, make dragon-bone water wheels, dig shaded wells, and erect well-shelf frames, all issuing models for imitation.
translations.idiomatic: Well aware that Guangxi's terrain was like water in a tilted jar—ten days without rain and drought followed—he urged the people to repair dikes and ponds, build dragon-bone water wheels, dig shaded wells, and erect well-shelf frames, issuing models for each so they could be copied everywhere.

sentences.zh: 地連黔、楚，群盜出沒，宜山會匪廖五桂、藍耀青分踞新、舊兩墟，糾眾分黨，偽立名目，勒索殷戶，爭利相擾，親往捕誅之。

translations.literal: The region bordered Guizhou and Huguang; bandits came and went. At Yishan, Heaven and Earth Society bandits Liao Wugui and Lan Yaoqing held the new and old market sites respectively, gathering followers in factions with false titles, extorting wealthy households and fighting over profits—he went in person and captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Guizhou and Huguang, and bandits roamed freely. At Yishan, Heaven and Earth Society bandits Liao Wugui and Lan Yaoqing held the new and old market towns, mustering followers in rival factions under false titles, extorting wealthy households and fighting over spoils—Shenzhen went in person and captured and executed them.

sentences.zh: 飭屬行保甲，置望樓，練民壯互相守望，縣建卡房數十座，府各督屬會營巡緝。

translations.literal: He ordered subordinates to implement baojia, set watch towers, train local militia for mutual lookout, and built dozens of checkpoint houses in each county; each prefecture supervised subordinates jointly with garrison troops for patrol.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his subordinates to enforce the baojia system, erect watch towers, and train local militia for mutual defense; each county built dozens of checkpoint stations, and each prefecture supervised its subordinates in joint patrols with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 柳州至省千餘裡，設水汛四十三所，終任凡獲盜千七百餘人。

translations.literal: From Liuzhou to the provincial capital was more than a thousand li; he established forty-three river checkpoints, and throughout his tenure captured more than seventeen hundred bandits in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Liuzhou to the provincial capital was more than a thousand li; he established forty-three river checkpoints, and over his entire term captured more than seventeen hundred bandits.

sentences.zh: 盜多出於流匪，編客民籍，驅其單身遊蕩者，礦廠窯榨傭丁皆立冊，有保者留，否則逐。

translations.literal: Most bandits came from roaming fugitives; he registered guest populations, expelled rootless wanderers, and had mine and kiln workers all listed in registers—those with guarantors stayed, otherwise they were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Most bandits were roaming fugitives; he registered guest populations, expelled rootless drifters, and required all mine, kiln, and press workers to be entered in registers—those with guarantors could remain, the rest were expelled.

sentences.zh: 故事，梧、潯二關，巡撫例得動用盈餘。

translations.literal: By precedent, at the Wuzhou and Xunzhou custom houses the governor was entitled to use surplus funds.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, the governor was entitled to use surplus revenue from the Wuzhou and Xunzhou customs stations.

sentences.zh: 慎畛曰：「吾家衣食粗足，身為大臣，取盈將安用之？

translations.literal: Shenzhen said: "My family's food and clothing are roughly sufficient; as a great minister, what use would I have for surplus profits?
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhen said, "My family's food and clothing are already adequate; as a senior minister, what would I do with surplus profits?

sentences.zh: 當為國家布仁澤耳。

translations.literal: One ought to spread benevolent favor for the state."
translations.idiomatic: They ought to be used to spread the state's benevolence."

sentences.zh: 」乃於桂林設預備倉，增設書院，柳州、慶遠、思恩三府皆創設之；

translations.literal: Thereupon he established a reserve granary at Guilin, added academies, and founded them in Liuzhou, Qingyuan, and Sinan as well;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he established a reserve granary at Guilin, expanded the provincial academy, and founded new academies in Liuzhou, Qingyuan, and Sinan;

sentences.zh: 繕城濬河，廣置棲流所，並取給焉。

translations.literal: repaired city walls and dredged rivers, greatly expanded shelters for vagrants, and drew funds from these for all.
translations.idiomatic: repaired city walls and dredged rivers, greatly expanded shelters for the destitute, and drew on these funds for all of it.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，入覲，宣宗嘉其誠實不欺，溫諭褒勉，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he entered court audience; the Xuanzong Emperor praised his honesty without deceit, warmly encouraged him, and promoted him to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daoguang he had an audience with the throne; the Daoguang Emperor praised his honesty and sincerity, spoke warmly in encouragement, and promoted him to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嚴申軍律，課諸鎮營汛勤訓練。

translations.literal: He strictly enforced military discipline and pressed the garrisons and posts to train diligently.
translations.idiomatic: He strictly enforced military discipline and pressed every garrison and post to train diligently.

sentences.zh: 浙江提督沈添華玩縱，劾罷之。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang provincial military commander Shen Tianhua was indulgent and lax; he impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang provincial commander Shen Tianhua was negligent and indulgent; Shenzhen impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 責水師緝海盜，盜多就擒。

translations.literal: He charged the navy to suppress pirates at sea; many pirates were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the navy to hunt down sea pirates, and many were captured.

sentences.zh: 上游四府多山，客民租山立廠，遊匪群聚，遣兵搜山，捕誅其魁。

translations.literal: The four upper prefectures were mostly mountainous; guest tenants rented mountains for mines, and roaming bandits gathered; he sent troops to search the mountains and captured and executed the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The four upstream prefectures were mountainous; migrant tenants rented hillsides for mines and roaming bandits gathered there; he sent troops to sweep the mountains and captured and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 閩安所轄有瑯琦島，居民多為奸利，擒治之，移駐水師，建砲台，遂為省城門戶。

translations.literal: Under Min'an jurisdiction was Langqi Island, whose inhabitants mostly pursued illicit profit; he arrested and punished them, moved naval forces there, built batteries, and it became the gateway of the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Min'an jurisdiction lay Langqi Island, whose inhabitants mostly pursued illicit gain; he arrested and punished them, stationed naval forces there, built batteries, and turned the island into the gateway of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 台灣自來多亂，動煩大兵，慎畛尤以為慮，盡選賢能以治。

translations.literal: Taiwan had long been prone to unrest, often requiring large military campaigns—Shenzhen was especially concerned and selected worthy men to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan had long been turbulent and often required large military expeditions; Shenzhen was especially concerned about this and selected the ablest officials he could find to govern it.

sentences.zh: 鳳山莠民楊良斌煽眾起事，檄巡道孔昭虔、知府孔傳穟剿治，未一月而定，不煩一兵渡海。

translations.literal: The unruly townsman Yang Liangbin of Fengshan incited the masses to rise; he ordered the circuit intendant Kong Zhaoqian and prefect Kong Chuansui to suppress it, and within a month it was settled without a single soldier crossing the sea.
translations.idiomatic: A troublemaker of Fengshan named Yang Liangbin incited a popular uprising; Shenzhen dispatched orders to the circuit intendant Kong Zhaoqian and the prefect Kong Chuansui to suppress it, and within a month the affair was settled without a single soldier crossing the strait.

sentences.zh: 驩瑪蘭初設治，部議賦則較重，奏減之。

translations.literal: Huanmalan had only recently been placed under administration; the ministry had set heavier tax rates—he memorialized for reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Huanmalan had only recently been brought under civil administration; the Board had set comparatively heavy tax rates, and he memorialized for their reduction.

sentences.zh: 民入山伐木，歲供道廠船料，匠首苛斂激變，捕誅首亂，更定採木章程，乃相安。

translations.literal: When people entered the mountains to cut timber, they yearly supplied ship timber for the circuit factory; the master craftsmen's harsh levies provoked unrest—he captured and executed the ringleaders, revised regulations for timber cutting, and peace was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the people went into the mountains to cut timber they supplied shipbuilding timber to the circuit yard each year; the head craftsmen's harsh exactions provoked an uprising—he captured and executed the ringleaders, revised the regulations for timber cutting, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 戍兵萬四千，更代時皆赴廈門，由提督點驗，遠者千里，改由各提鎮分驗，兵困以蘇。

translations.literal: Garrison troops numbered fourteen thousand; when rotated they all went to Xiamen for inspection by the provincial commander—some traveled a thousand li—so he changed it so each commander inspected separately, and the troops' hardship was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: There were fourteen thousand garrison troops; when rotations came due they all had to report to Xiamen for inspection by the provincial commander, and some traveled a thousand li—he changed the rule so each regional commander inspected his own men locally, and the soldiers' hardship was eased.

sentences.zh: 台灣產米，漳、泉數郡仰給商運，江、浙、天津民無蓋藏，米貴輒生亂，於海口稽米船出數，酌豐歉為限制，常留有餘。

translations.literal: Taiwan produced rice; Zhangzhou and Quanzhou prefectures depended on commercial transport; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Tianjin commoners had no reserves, and when rice was dear unrest arose—at seaports he tallied rice ships departing, adjusted restrictions according to harvest abundance or shortage, and always kept a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan produced rice on which Zhangzhou and Quanzhou depended through merchant shipping; in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Tianjin the people had no reserves, and dearth of rice often sparked unrest—at the seaports he tallied rice exports, adjusted limits according to harvest conditions, and always kept a reserve on hand.

sentences.zh: 疏請漳浦明儒黃道周從祀文廟，下廷臣議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Ming scholar Huang Daozhou of Zhangpu should be admitted to the Confucian temple; the court's ministers deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the Ming scholar Huang Daozhou of Zhangpu should be admitted to the Confucian temple; the memorial was referred to the court for deliberation and carried out.

sentences.zh: 侯官謝金鑾、德化鄭兼才皆以學行著，素所敬禮，歿而舉祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: Xie Jinzuan of Houguan and Zheng Jian'ai of Dehua were both renowned for learning and conduct, whom he had long respected; when they died he recommended them for worship in local worthy shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jinzuan of Houguan and Zheng Jian'ai of Dehua were both renowned for learning and moral conduct and had long been men he honored; when they died he recommended them for worship in the local worthies' shrines.

sentences.zh: 又旌表義烈，以振風俗。

translations.literal: He also honored righteous martyrs to uplift custom.
translations.idiomatic: He also honored the righteous and the martyred to uplift public morals.

sentences.zh: 五年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 銅礦、鹽務積疲，疏陳變通整頓之法。

translations.literal: Copper mines and salt administration had long been exhausted; he memorialized methods for flexible overhaul.
translations.idiomatic: Copper mining and the salt monopoly had long been in decline; he memorialized methods for flexible reform and consolidation.

sentences.zh: 以邊防莫便於屯田，方考訪形勢利便，未及議行而疾作。

translations.literal: For border defense, garrison farming was the most convenient; he was investigating terrain and advantages but had not yet memorialized implementation when illness struck.
translations.idiomatic: Believing that garrison farming was the best means of border defense, he was still surveying terrain and advantages when illness struck before he could submit his proposals.

sentences.zh: 病中拜疏劾貪黷不職者數十人。

translations.literal: While ill he presented a memorial impeaching several dozen greedy and negligent officials.
translations.idiomatic: From his sickbed he submitted a memorial impeaching several dozen corrupt and negligent officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 代者急遞追回原疏，滇人惜之。

translations.literal: His successor urgently recalled the original memorial by express relay; the people of Yunnan regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: His successor urgently recalled the original memorial by express relay; the people of Yunnan deeply regretted the loss.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，優詔賜卹，贈太子少保，諡文恪，祀名宦、鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: His death memorial was submitted; an edict graciously granted condolence payments, posthumously appointed him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave the posthumous title Wenge, and enshrined him in shrines to famous officials and local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When his death memorial reached the throne, an edict graciously granted funeral honors, posthumously appointed him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave him the posthumous title Wenge, and ordered his enshrinement in the shrines of eminent officials and local worthies.

sentences.zh: 慎畛服膺儒先，凡有益身心可致用者，皆身體力行。

translations.literal: Shenzhen embraced the Confucian sages; whatever benefited body and mind and could be applied in practice, he practiced in person.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhen devoted himself to the Confucian sages; whatever could benefit mind and body and be put to practical use, he practiced in his own person.

sentences.zh: 好善嫉惡，體恤屬僚，訓懇切，如師之於弟子。

translations.literal: He loved the good and hated evil, was considerate to subordinates, and instructed them earnestly like a teacher with pupils.
translations.idiomatic: He loved virtue and hated vice, was considerate toward his subordinates, and instructed them earnestly, like a teacher with his pupils.

sentences.zh: 所至於文武官吏，常能識別其才否，人亦樂為之用。

translations.literal: Wherever he went among civil and military officials, he could usually discern their capacity; people were also glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he could usually discern the abilities of civil and military officials, and men were glad to work for him.

sentences.zh: 所著奏議、從征錄、載年錄、讀書日記、惜日筆記等書及詩文集凡數十卷。

translations.literal: His collected memorials, campaigns record, year-by-year record, reading diary, notes on cherishing time, and other books plus poetry and prose totaled several dozen fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His writings—including memorials, a campaign record, a chronological memoir, a reading diary, notes on cherishing time, and collected poetry and prose—amounted to several dozen fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 盧坤，字厚山，順天涿州人。

translations.literal: Lu Kun, styled Houshan, was a man of Zhuozhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kun, whose courtesy name was Houshan, came from Zhuozhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士，散館授兵部主事，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, after leaving the academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of War, and rose steadily to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of War, rising steadily to director.

sentences.zh: 扈隨木蘭，校射，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Attending the emperor at Mulan, in archery competition he received the gift of a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: While attending the emperor on the Mulan hunt he distinguished himself in archery and was granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十八年，出為湖南糧儲道，丁本生父母憂，服闋，歷廣東惠潮嘉道、山東兗沂曹濟道、湖北按察使、甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he went out as grain intendant of Hunan; upon the death of his adoptive mother he mourned; after mourning he served as intendant of Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiazhou in Guangdong, intendant of Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji in Shandong, provincial judge of Hubei, and provincial treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was posted as grain intendant of Hunan; after mourning his adoptive mother he served successively as intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiazhou circuit in Guangdong, intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji circuit in Shandong, provincial judge of Hubei, and provincial treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，護理陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he acted as governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he served as acting governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢廣東巡撫，未之任，調陝西。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong but did not take up the post, being transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong but never took up the post, being transferred instead to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 議者謂南山老林易藪姦，不宜開墾。

translations.literal: Critics said the old forests of the southern mountains easily harbored villains and should not be opened for reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that the old forests of the southern mountains easily sheltered bandits and ought not to be opened for reclamation.

sentences.zh: 坤歷陳漢、蜀、唐、宋史事，及漢李翕郙閣頌，以徵墾治之利；

translations.literal: Kun cited repeatedly events from Han, Shu, Tang, and Song histories, and Han Li Xi's Efu Pavilion inscription, to demonstrate the benefits of reclamation;
translations.idiomatic: Kun cited one historical precedent after another from the histories of Han, Shu, Tang, and Song, as well as Li Xi's Han inscription on the Efu Pavilion, to demonstrate the benefits of reclamation;

sentences.zh: 專任嚴如熤，假以便宜，墾務大興。

translations.literal: he put Yan Ruyi solely in charge with discretionary authority, and reclamation flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: he put Yan Ruyi solely in charge with full discretionary authority, and reclamation work flourished.

sentences.zh: 勘修南山各屬城工，漢江堤岸，築壩濬淤，審度形勢，移駐文武，增改官制。

translations.literal: He surveyed and repaired city works in various districts of the southern mountains, Han River dikes, built dams and dredged silt, assessed terrain, relocated civil and military officials, and revised the official establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed and repaired city fortifications throughout the southern mountain districts, strengthened the Han River dikes, built dams and dredged silt, assessed the terrain, redeployed civil and military officials, and revised the local administrative structure.

sentences.zh: 又修復咸寧、長安、涇陽、盩厔、岐山、寶雞、華州、榆林河渠水利，籌補榆林、綏德兩屬常平倉穀，勸民捐建社倉。

translations.literal: He also restored river conservancy in Xianning, Chang'an, Jingyang, Zhouzhi, Qishan, Baoji, Huazhou, and Yulin, replenished ever-normal granary grain in Yulin and Suide prefectures, and urged the people to donate and build community granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also restored irrigation works in Xianning, Chang'an, Jingyang, Zhouzhi, Qishan, Baoji, Huazhou, and Yulin, replenished the ever-normal granaries of Yulin and Suide, and urged the people to donate grain and establish community granaries.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「察吏之要，不獨親民，官貪廉為民身家所繫，其勤​​惰、明昧、寬嚴，皆關民生休戚。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The key to inspecting officials lies not only in closeness to the people—for an official's probity or corruption is tied to the people's livelihood; their diligence or sloth, clarity or obscurity, leniency or severity all affect the people's weal and woe.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The key to inspecting officials is not merely whether they are close to the people—an official's probity or corruption is bound up with the people's livelihood, and his diligence or sloth, clarity or obtuseness, leniency or severity all bear on their welfare.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗深韙之。

translations.literal: " The Xuanzong Emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Daoguang Emperor strongly approved his view.

sentences.zh: 五年，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，回疆用兵，特起駐肅州，偕總督鄂山治轉餉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when troops were sent to the western regions, he was specially summoned to station at Suzhou and together with Governor-General E Shan managed transport of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the campaign in the western regions began, he was specially recalled from mourning to station at Suzhou and, together with Governor-General E Shan, managed the transport of supplies.

sentences.zh: 以托古遜為運糧首站，自烏魯木齊至阿克蘇，置三十二站，大兵五萬餘，日需糧五百石，每站備駝五百有奇，由山西、陝西採購；

translations.literal: Taking Tuogusiun as the first grain station, from Urumqi to Aksu he established thirty-two stations; the main army of over fifty thousand required five hundred shi of grain daily; each station prepared over five hundred camels, procured from Shanxi and Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: With Tuogusiun as the first grain depot, he established thirty-two relay stations from Urumqi to Aksu; the main force of more than fifty thousand men required five hundred shi of grain a day, and each station was supplied with over five hundred camels purchased from Shanxi and Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 又蒙古阿拉善部進駝千，烏里雅蘇台調撥官駝四千。

translations.literal: also a thousand camels from the Alashan Mongols, and four thousand government camels transferred from Uliassutai.
translations.idiomatic: in addition, a thousand camels were contributed by the Alashan Mongols, and four thousand government camels were transferred from Uliassutai.

sentences.zh: 疏請軍需從寬籌備；

translations.literal: He memorialized that military supplies should be prepared generously;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that military supplies should be prepared generously;

sentences.zh: 兵丁量增口糧；

translations.literal: soldiers' rations should be increased as appropriate;
translations.idiomatic: soldiers' rations should be increased as needed;

sentences.zh: 給皮衣皮帽，以御寒；

translations.literal: fur coats and hats given against the cold;
translations.idiomatic: fur coats and hats issued against the cold;

sentences.zh: 出口駝馬芻秣；

translations.literal: fodder for camels and horses at relay stations;
translations.idiomatic: fodder supplied for camels and horses along the route;

sentences.zh: 時給買補缺額營馬，預備續調；

translations.literal: at times funds to buy replacements for deficient camp horses, preparing for further transfers;
translations.idiomatic: periodic funds to purchase replacements for camp horses lost on campaign, in preparation for further deployments;

sentences.zh: 監造軍械務期堅實；

translations.literal: oversight of arms manufacture to ensure solidity;
translations.idiomatic: strict supervision of arms manufacture to ensure durability;

sentences.zh: 撥運陝省制錢，平市價；

translations.literal: transport of Shaanxi minted cash to stabilize market prices;
translations.idiomatic: shipment of Shaanxi minted cash to stabilize market prices;

sentences.zh: 添設台站夫馬；

translations.literal: additional relay station couriers and horses;
translations.idiomatic: additional couriers and horses at relay stations;

sentences.zh: 僱用車輛，定例價；

translations.literal: hired carts at fixed regulated prices;
translations.idiomatic: hired transport at fixed regulated rates;

sentences.zh: 招募護台民丁；

translations.literal: recruitment of civilians to guard relay stations;
translations.idiomatic: recruitment of civilian guards for relay stations;

sentences.zh: 後路糧台亦添兵守護：凡十一事，並如議行。

translations.literal: rear supply depots also given added military guards—all eleven items were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: added troops to guard the rear supply depots as well—all eleven proposals were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 回疆平，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the western regions were pacified, he was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the western regions were pacified, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及張格爾就擒，賜頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: When Zhang Ge'er was captured, he was granted the first-grade finial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ge'er was captured, he was granted the first-grade finial.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授山東巡撫，調山西。

translations.literal: After mourning he was appointed governor of Shandong, then transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his mourning period he was appointed governor of Shandong, then transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，裁撤肅州軍局。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Suzhou military supply bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Suzhou military supply bureau was abolished.

sentences.zh: 始抵任，尋調廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: He had just arrived when he was soon transferred to governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely taken up his post when he was transferred to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十年，又調江蘇，未至，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred again to Jiangsu, but before arriving was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu, but before he could take up the post he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 兩湖鹺務，狃於封輪之例，道光初議散輪，七年復因加價，仍改封輪，引滯商疲。

translations.literal: Salt affairs in the two lakes were wedded to the sealed-lot system; in early Daoguang scattered lots were discussed, but in the seventh year because of price increases they reverted to sealed lots, causing stagnation and merchant exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Salt administration in the two Hu had long clung to the sealed-lot system; in early Daoguang open lots were proposed, but in the seventh year price increases led to a return to sealed lots, causing stagnation and exhausting the merchants.

sentences.zh: 坤至，疏請實行散輪，建鹽倉於漢岸，俾商船源源攬運。

translations.literal: When Kun arrived, he memorialized to implement scattered lots in earnest, built salt warehouses on the Han shore, so merchant boats could transport continuously.
translations.idiomatic: When Kun arrived he memorialized to implement open lots in earnest, built salt warehouses on the Han River shore, and enabled merchant boats to transport salt in a steady stream.

sentences.zh: 尋量減售價，以銷楚岸積鹽。

translations.literal: Soon he reduced selling prices proportionally to clear accumulated salt on the Chu bank.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reduced selling prices in proportion to clear the accumulated salt stocks on the Chu River bank.

sentences.zh: 設塘角總卡，按船編號，以杜內私外私之弊。

translations.literal: He set up a master checkpoint at Tangjiao, numbered boats by registry, to stop internal and external smuggling abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He established a master checkpoint at Tangjiao and registered boats by number to stop both internal and external smuggling.

sentences.zh: 复湖南永興粵鹽定額，以保淮綱。

translations.literal: He restored the fixed Guangdong salt quota for Yongxing in Hunan to protect the Huai salt monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the fixed Guangdong salt quota for Yongxing in Hunan to protect the Huai salt monopoly zone.

sentences.zh: 湖北水災，請免米稅，借帑十萬兩，購川米平糶。

translations.literal: When Hubei suffered flood, he requested exemption of rice taxes, borrowed one hundred thousand taels from the treasury, and purchased Sichuan rice for sale at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: When Hubei was struck by flooding he requested exemption of rice taxes, borrowed one hundred thousand taels from the treasury, and purchased Sichuan rice for sale at fair prices to the people.

sentences.zh: 疏調前兩淮鹽運使王鳳生綜理水利，擇要疏濬河道，修築堤堰，皆以次舉行。

translations.literal: He memorialized to transfer the former Lianghuai salt transport commissioner Wang Fengsheng to oversee water conservancy comprehensively, selecting key points to dredge rivers and repair dikes and dams, all carried out in due order.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to assign the former Lianghuai salt transport commissioner Wang Fengsheng to oversee water conservancy, selecting the most critical points for river dredging and dike repair, all of which were carried out in turn.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖南江華瑤趙金龍作亂，粵瑤應之，湖南提督海凌阿及副將、游擊等皆戰歿，坤親往督師，密陳湖北提督羅思舉能辦賊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zhao Jinlong, a Yao of Jianghua in Hunan, rebelled, and Yao in Guangdong responded; Hunan provincial commander Hailing'a and vice commanders, brigade commanders, and others all died in battle. Kun went in person to direct the army and secretly memorialized that Hubei provincial commander Luo Siju was capable of handling the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua in Hunan rose in rebellion, and Yao in Guangdong rose in response; the Hunan provincial commander Hailing'a and his vice commanders and brigade officers were all killed in battle. Kun went in person to take command and secretly memorialized that the Hubei provincial commander Luo Siju was the man to defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時桂陽、常德諸瑤蜂起應賊，常德水師、荊州駐防兵皆不習山戰，坤至，悉罷之，改調鎮筸苗疆兵，分屯要隘，堅壁清野，與賊相持。

translations.literal: At that time Yao in Guiyang, Changde, and elsewhere rose in response to the rebels; Changde naval forces and garrison troops from Jingzhou were unused to mountain warfare—when Kun arrived he dismissed them all, transferred Zhenxiong Miao frontier troops, garrisoned strategic passes, practiced fortified defense and scorched earth, and held the enemy at bay.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yao in Guiyang, Changde, and other districts rose in support of the rebels; the Changde naval forces and the Jingzhou garrison troops were unskilled in mountain warfare—when Kun arrived he dismissed them all, transferred troops from the Zhenxiong Miao frontier, garrisoned the strategic passes, practiced scorched-earth defense, and held the rebels at bay.

sentences.zh: 俟兩湖兵大集，貴州提督餘步雲、雲南副將曾勝亦率軍至，乘雷雨襲擊洋泉街。

translations.literal: When forces from both lakes had gathered in strength, Guizhou provincial commander Yu Buyun and Yunnan vice commander Zeng Sheng also led troops; taking advantage of thunder and rain they attacked Yangquan Street.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of the two Hu had massed in strength, the Guizhou provincial commander Yu Buyun and the Yunnan vice commander Zeng Sheng also brought their forces; they took advantage of a thunderstorm to strike Yangquan Street.

sentences.zh: 羅思舉督諸將晝夜環攻，斃賊數千，破其巢，擒金龍子女及頭目數百人。

translations.literal: Luo Siju directed the generals in day-and-night encirclement assault, killing several thousand rebels, breaking their nest, and capturing Jinlong's children and several hundred ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Siju directed the generals in round-the-clock encirclement attacks, killing several thousand rebels, destroying their stronghold, and capturing Jinlong's children and several hundred subordinate leaders.

sentences.zh: 金龍乘間逸，為亂軍所殲，獲其屍及劍印木偶諸物。

translations.literal: Jinlong slipped away in the chaos and was killed by his own disorderly troops; his corpse and sword, seals, wooden idols, and other items were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlong slipped away in the confusion and was killed by his own disorderly troops; his corpse was recovered along with his sword, seals, wooden idols, and other objects.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜雙眼花翎，世襲一等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: On report of victory he was granted double-eyed peacock feather and hereditary first-rank light chariot commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When news of victory arrived he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and a hereditary rank as first-class light chariot commandant.

sentences.zh: 尚書禧恩、將軍瑚松額方奉命視師，未至，賊已平。

translations.literal: Minister Xien and General Husong'e had been ordered to inspect the army but had not arrived when the rebels were already suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The minister Xien and the general Husong'e had been ordered to take command of the campaign, but before they arrived the rebels had already been suppressed.

sentences.zh: 粵瑤趙青仔糾眾數千入楚界，聲言為金龍復仇，連敗之於濠江、銀江，擒青仔磔於市。

translations.literal: Guangdong Yao Zhao Qingzai gathered several thousand men into Hunan territory claiming revenge for Jinlong; they were repeatedly defeated at Haojiang and Yinjiang; Qingzai was captured and dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong Yao leader Zhao Qingzai mustered several thousand men and crossed into Hunan, claiming to avenge Jinlong; he was repeatedly defeated at Haojiang and Yinjiang, captured, and dismembered in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 廣東連山黃瓜寨瑤猶猖獗，兩廣總督李鴻賓剿治不力，以罪逮，調坤代之。

translations.literal: Huangguazhai Yao in Lianshan, Guangdong, were still rampant; Liangguang governor-general Li Hongbin's suppression was ineffective and he was arrested for crime; Kun was transferred to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao of Huangguazhai in Lianshan, Guangdong, were still rampant; Governor-General Li Hongbin's campaign against them had failed, and he was arrested on criminal charges; Kun was transferred to replace him.

sentences.zh: 偕禧恩等先後往督諸將進剿，瑤疆悉平。

translations.literal: Together with Xien and others he went in succession to direct the generals in suppression, and the Yao regions were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xien and others he went in turn to direct the generals in the campaign, and the Yao territories were entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 合疏陳兩省善後事宜，改移文武官制駐所，並允行。

translations.literal: In a joint memorial they set forth post-pacification affairs for both provinces, relocating civil and military posts—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: In a joint memorial they laid out post-pacification measures for both provinces, including the relocation of civil and military posts—all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 十三年，越南盜陳加海結邊地遊民嘯聚狗頭山，潛入內洋，遣水師擊沉八船，擒加海誅之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Vietnamese bandit Chen Jiahai joined border vagabonds and gathered at Goutoushan, secretly entering inner waters; he dispatched naval forces to sink eight ships and captured and executed Jiahai.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Vietnamese pirate Chen Jiahai joined with border vagabonds and gathered at Goutoushan, secretly entering coastal waters; Kun dispatched the navy, sank eight of their ships, captured Jiahai, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 尋越南內訌，慎固邊防，拒其請兵，詔嘉得大體。

translations.literal: Soon Vietnam had internal strife; he firmly guarded the border and refused their request for troops; an edict praised his grasp of essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Vietnam fell into civil strife; he firmly guarded the frontier and refused their request for military aid; an edict praised his grasp of the larger situation.

sentences.zh: 英吉利兵船擅入海口，要乞推廣通商，坤依故事停其貿易。

translations.literal: English warships intruded into the estuary demanding expanded trade; Kun according to precedent suspended their trade.
translations.idiomatic: English warships entered the estuary without authorization and demanded expanded trade; Kun, following established precedent, suspended their commerce.

sentences.zh: 領事律勞卑挾二船入虎門，砲擊不退，且以砲拒，進泊黃埔。

translations.literal: Consul Napier forced two ships into Humen; cannon fire did not drive them back, and they used cannon to resist, advancing to anchor at Huangpu.
translations.idiomatic: The consul Napier forced two ships into Humen; cannon fire failed to drive them back, and they returned fire with their own guns before advancing to anchor at Huangpu.

sentences.zh: 坤設方略扼其歸路，斷其接濟，集水陸師臨以兵威，律勞卑窮蹙，引罪求去。

translations.literal: Kun devised plans to block their return route and cut off supplies, assembled land and naval forces to overawe them with military might; Napier in dire straits confessed guilt and begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Kun devised a strategy to block their line of retreat and cut off their supplies, assembled land and naval forces to overawe them, and Napier, cornered, confessed his offense and begged to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 澳門洋商代請命，坤持之良久，乃驅之出口。

translations.literal: Macao foreign merchants pleaded on his behalf; Kun held firm for a long time before driving them out of port.
translations.idiomatic: Macao merchants interceded on Napier's behalf; Kun held firm for a long time before finally driving the ships out of port.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，詔嘉獎，先奪宮銜、花翎並復之。

translations.literal: The memorial was reported; an edict praised and rewarded him, first stripping then restoring rank insignia and peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict praised and rewarded him, having first stripped and then restored his rank insignia and peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 於是嚴海防，勤訓練，自南山至大虎分三段，與沙角、大角相聯絡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he strictly guarded coastal defense and diligently trained; from Nanshan to Dahu he divided into three sections linked with Shajiao and Dajiao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he tightened coastal defenses and pressed training; from Nanshan to Dahu he divided the coast into three sections linked with Shajiao and Dajiao.

sentences.zh: 省河中流沙地增建砲台，以資保障，夷情斂懾。

translations.literal: On sandy shoals in the provincial river channel he added batteries for protection; foreign attitude became restrained.
translations.idiomatic: He built additional batteries on the shifting sandbanks in the provincial river channel for added protection, and foreign conduct became noticeably restrained.

sentences.zh: 坤久任封圻，所皆有名績，宣宗深倚之。

translations.literal: Kun long held frontier posts with notable achievements everywhere; the Xuanzong Emperor deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Kun had long held high provincial office with distinguished achievements wherever he served, and the Daoguang Emperor relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒，贈太子太師、兵部尚書，從優恤，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, generous condolence, posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died; he was posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, granted generous funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子端黼，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Duandian inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duandian inherited the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 曾勝，廣西馬平人。

translations.literal: Zeng Sheng was a man of Maping in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Sheng came from Maping in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 以行伍從剿湖南苗匪、川、楚教匪，積功至都司。

translations.literal: From military rank he followed suppression of Hunan Miao bandits and Sichuan-Huguang secret sect rebels, accumulating merit to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks, he took part in suppressing Miao bandits in Hunan and the secret-society rebels of Sichuan and Huguang, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of commandant.

sentences.zh: 累遷雲南參將，以計擒梟渠徐黑二及宣威小梁山匪首，為時稱。

translations.literal: He rose to Yunnan colonel; by stratagem he captured ringleaders Xu Hei'er and the Xuanwei Xiaoliangshan bandit chief—acclaimed at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel in Yunnan; by stratagem he captured the ringleader Xu Hei'er and the bandit chief of Xiaoliangshan in Xuanwei, winning acclaim at the time.

sentences.zh: 遷維西協副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Weixi brigade vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commander of the Weixi brigade.

sentences.zh: 瑤匪趙金龍之亂，率師會剿，擢湖南永州鎮總兵，殲金龍，及擒粵瑤趙青仔，戰皆力。

translations.literal: In Zhao Jinlong's Yao rebellion he led troops in joint suppression, was promoted to Yongzhou garrison commander of Hunan, exterminated Jinlong, and captured Guangdong Yao Zhao Qingzai—he fought with vigor in all.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yao rebellion of Zhao Jinlong he led troops in the joint campaign, was promoted to commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan, destroyed Jinlong, and captured the Guangdong Yao leader Zhao Qingzai—fighting with great vigor in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 尋赴廣東剿連山瑤，迭戰大拱橋、分水嶺、砲台山、火燒坪、軍僚裡、大厓衝、上坻園。

translations.literal: Soon he went to Guangdong to suppress Lianshan Yao, fighting repeatedly at Dagong Bridge, Fenshuiling, Paotaishan, Huoshaoping, Junliaoli, Dayachong, and Shangdiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to Guangdong to suppress the Lianshan Yao, fighting successive battles at Dagong Bridge, Fenshuiling, Paotaishan, Huoshaoping, Junliaoli, Dayachong, and Shangdiyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑤平，論功最，加提督銜，賜號瑚爾察圖巴圖魯，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When the Yao were pacified his merit was judged greatest; he was given provincial commander rank, granted the title Hurcitu Baturu, and a Yunqiwei hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao were pacified his merit was judged the greatest; he was given the rank of provincial commander, granted the title Hurcitu Baturu, and awarded a hereditary Yunqiwei office.

sentences.zh: 調南韶連鎮，擢廣東陸路提督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Nanshaolian garrison and promoted to Guangdong provincial ground forces commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Nanshaolian garrison and promoted to provincial commander of Guangdong's land forces.

sentences.zh: 當英吉利兵船入內河，水師提督李增堦不能阻，勝獻策，以巨船載石沉塞海口老洲岡隘道，聚草船數百橫內河，備火攻，勝率兵臨之，英領事律勞卑悚懼聽令，事乃定。

translations.literal: When English warships entered the inner river, naval commander Li Zengjie could not block them; Sheng offered a plan—great ships loaded with stone to block the Haikou Laozhougang pass, hundreds of straw boats placed across the inner river for fire attack; Sheng led troops pressing them; English consul Napier in fear obeyed orders, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When English warships entered the inner river the naval commander Li Zengjie could not stop them; Sheng proposed loading great ships with stone to block the Laozhougang pass at the estuary, assembling hundreds of straw boats across the inner river for a fire attack, and leading troops to press them; the English consul Napier, fearful, submitted to orders, and the crisis was resolved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於官，諡勤勇。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died in office; posthumous title Qinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died in office and was given the posthumous title Qinyong.

sentences.zh: 陶澍，字云汀，湖南安化人。

translations.literal: Tao Shu, styled Yunting, was a man of Anhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shu, whose courtesy name was Yunting, came from Anhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler, and was promoted to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏劾吏部重簽，河工冒濫，及外省吏治積弊。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeachment of the Board of Civil Office for duplicate signatures, fraud in river works, and accumulated abuses in provincial governance.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against duplicate signatures in the Board of Civil Office, fraud in river conservancy projects, and long-standing abuses in provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 巡中城，決滯獄八百有奇。

translations.literal: Patrolling the central city, he resolved more than eight hundred stagnant cases.
translations.idiomatic: While patrolling the central city he cleared more than eight hundred backlogged cases.

sentences.zh: 巡南漕，革陋規，請濬京口運河。

translations.literal: Patrolling southern grain transport, he abolished corrupt customs and requested dredging the Jingkou transport canal.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting southern grain transport he abolished entrenched abuses and petitioned to dredge the Jingkou transport canal.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，出為川東道，日坐堂皇，剖決獄訟如流。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he went out as intendant of eastern Sichuan, daily sitting in the hall and deciding lawsuits like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was posted as intendant of eastern Sichuan, sitting daily in court and dispatching lawsuits with remarkable fluency.

sentences.zh: 請減鹽價，私絕課增。

translations.literal: He requested reduction of salt prices and privately ended tax increases.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to reduce salt prices and on his own authority halted unauthorized tax increases.

sentences.zh: 總督蔣攸銛薦其治行為四川第一。

translations.literal: Governor-General Jiang Youxian recommended his governance as first in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Jiang Youxian recommended his administration as the finest in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 歷山西按察使、安徽布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Shanxi provincial judge and Anhui provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as provincial judge of Shanxi and provincial treasurer of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he was directly promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang he was promoted directly to governor.

sentences.zh: 安徽庫款，五次清查，未得要領。

translations.literal: Anhui treasury funds had been audited five times without reaching conclusions.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui's treasury accounts had been audited five times without reaching a clear resolution.

sentences.zh: 澍自為籓司時，鉤覈檔案，分別應劾、應償、應豁，於是三十餘年之糾轕，豁然一清。

translations.literal: When Shu was provincial treasurer he audited archives, distinguishing what should be impeached, compensated, or remitted; thus more than thirty years of entanglements were suddenly cleared.
translations.idiomatic: While still provincial treasurer Shu audited the archives, distinguishing cases requiring impeachment, repayment, or remission, and thereby cleared away more than thirty years of accumulated entanglements at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 嚴交代，禁流攤，裁捐款，至是奏定章程，俾有司釋累，得專力治民。

translations.literal: He strictly enforced handover of accounts, banned spreading levies, and cut donations; at this time he memorialized fixed regulations so officials could shed burdens and devote themselves to governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced strict account handovers, banned spreading levies among the people, and cut unauthorized donations; he then memorialized fixed regulations so that local officials could shed their burdens and devote themselves wholly to governing the people.

sentences.zh: 瀕江水災，購米十萬石，勸捐數十萬金，賑務覈實，災民賴之無失所。

translations.literal: Along the river there was flood; he purchased one hundred thousand shi of rice, urged donations of several hundred thousand taels, verified relief accounts, and disaster victims relied on this without losing their homes.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck along the Yangzi he purchased one hundred thousand shi of rice, urged donations totaling several hundred thousand taels, verified relief accounts rigorously, and the disaster victims were saved from destitution.

sentences.zh: 治壽州城西湖、鳳臺蕉岡湖、鳳陽花源湖；

translations.literal: He managed the West Lake at Shouzhou city, Jiaogang Lake at Fengtai, and Huayuan Lake at Fengyang;
translations.idiomatic: He undertook works on the West Lake at Shouzhou, Jiaogang Lake at Fengtai, and Huayuan Lake at Fengyang;

sentences.zh: 又懷遠新漲沙洲阻水，並開引河，導之入淮。

translations.literal: also at Huaiyuan newly formed sandbars blocked the water; he opened diversion channels to guide it into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: at Huaiyuan, newly formed sandbars were blocking the water, so he opened diversion channels to guide it into the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 淮水所經，勸民修隄束水，保障農田。

translations.literal: Where the Huai River passed, he urged the people to repair dikes to contain the water and protect farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Along the course of the Huai he urged the people to repair dikes to contain the water and protect their farmland.

sentences.zh: 各縣設豐備倉於鄉村，令民秋收後量力分捐，不經吏役，不減糶，不出易，不假貸，歲歉備賑，樂歲再捐，略如社倉法而去其弊。

translations.literal: Each county established abundance reserve granaries in villages, ordering the people after autumn harvest to donate according to capacity, without going through clerks, without reducing sale prices, without exchange, without loans—in lean years for relief, in good years donating again, roughly like community granary methods but removing their abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In each county he established abundance reserve granaries in the villages, requiring the people after the autumn harvest to contribute according to their means without passing through clerks, without price reductions, exchange, or loans—in lean years the grain was used for relief, in good years they contributed again, following the community granary model but eliminating its abuses.

sentences.zh: 創輯安徽通志，旌表忠孝節烈以勵風俗。

translations.literal: He newly compiled the Anhui gazetteer and honored loyalty, filial piety, and chastity to encourage custom.
translations.idiomatic: He initiated compilation of the Anhui provincial gazetteer and honored the loyal, filial, and chaste to uplift public morals.

sentences.zh: 五年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 先是洪澤湖決，漕運梗阻，協辦大學士英和陳海運策，而中外紛議撓之。

translations.literal: Previously Hongze Lake had breached, obstructing grain transport; Grand Secretary Yinghe jointly proposed sea transport, but court and country debated and obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Hongze Lake dike had burst, blocking grain transport; the grand secretary Yinghe had jointly proposed sea transport, but debate at court and in the provinces frustrated the plan.

sentences.zh: 澍毅然以身任，奏請蘇、松、常、鎮、太五府州漕糧百六十餘萬石歸海運，親赴上海，籌僱商船，體恤商艱，群情踴躍。

translations.literal: Shu resolutely took personal responsibility, memorializing that grain tribute of more than 1.6 million shi from the five prefectures Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Taicang return to sea transport; he went in person to Shanghai, arranged hiring merchant ships, was considerate of merchants' hardships, and all were enthusiastic.
translations.idiomatic: Shu resolutely took personal responsibility, memorializing that the grain tribute of more than 1.6 million shi from Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Taicang be shifted to sea transport; he went in person to Shanghai, arranged the hiring of merchant vessels, showed consideration for the merchants' difficulties, and won widespread enthusiasm.

sentences.zh: 六年春，開兌，至夏全抵天津，無一漂損者，驗米色率瑩潔，過河運數倍。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year transport began; by summer all reached Tianjin without a single loss by flooding; inspected grain color was uniformly bright and clean, several times better than canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year shipping began; by summer the entire cargo had reached Tianjin without a single loss at sea; inspection showed the grain uniformly bright and clean, several times superior to canal transport.

sentences.zh: 商船回空，載豆而南，兩次得值船餘耗米十餘萬石，發部帑收買，由漕項協濟天津、通倉之用，及調劑旗丁，尚節省銀米各十餘萬。

translations.literal: Merchant ships returning empty carried beans south; twice they obtained more than one hundred thousand shi of surplus transport grain, purchased with ministry funds, used from grain tribute items to assist Tianjin and Tongzhou granaries and adjust banner soldiers' rations, still saving more than one hundred thousand taels and shi each of silver and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On their return voyages merchant ships carried beans southward; twice they brought back more than one hundred thousand shi of surplus transport grain, which was purchased with ministry funds and applied from grain-tribute revenues to supply Tianjin and Tongzhou granaries and adjust banner soldiers' rations, while still saving more than one hundred thousand taels of silver and shi of grain respectively.

sentences.zh: 事竣，優詔褒美，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded, an edict graciously praised him and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was completed, an edict warmly praised him and granted him a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂偕總督蔣攸銛合疏陳海運章程八條，冀垂令甲，永紓漕累，格於部議，未果行。

translations.literal: The next year he jointly with Governor-General Jiang Youxian memorialized eight articles of sea transport regulations, hoping to establish lasting precedent and permanently relieve grain tribute burdens; blocked by ministry deliberation, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he and Governor-General Jiang Youxian jointly memorialized eight articles governing sea transport, hoping to establish a lasting precedent and permanently ease the burden of the grain tribute system; the Board blocked the proposal and it was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 又以紳衿包完漕米，橫索陋規，為漕務之害，奏請懲辦。

translations.literal: Also, gentry who contracted to complete grain tribute extorted corrupt customs—a harm to grain transport affairs—he memorialized for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also found that gentry who contracted to deliver the grain tribute extorted illegal fees, a serious abuse of the transport system, and memorialized for their punishment.

sentences.zh: 學政辛從益意不合，爭之。

translations.literal: Educational commissioner Xin Congyi disagreed and disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: The educational commissioner Xin Congyi disagreed and argued against him.

sentences.zh: 澍复疏言：「陋規日增，勢必取償小民。

translations.literal: Shu again memorialized: "Corrupt customs increase daily; inevitably they will be recovered from the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized again: "These corrupt practices grow daily and will inevitably be recovered from the common people.

sentences.zh: 若預計有司不減浮收，置陋規於不問，非釜底抽薪之計。

translations.literal: If one assumes in advance that officials will not reduce excessive collection and leaves corrupt customs unaddressed, this is not a plan to remove fuel from under the cauldron."
translations.idiomatic: If we assume in advance that officials will not reduce excessive levies and leave these corrupt practices unaddressed, that is not a plan to remove the fuel from under the cauldron."

sentences.zh: 」仍執前議，治包抗從嚴焉。

translations.literal: " He still held to his earlier proposal and punished contractors who resisted strictly.
translations.idiomatic: " He held to his earlier proposal and punished contractors who resisted with severity.

sentences.zh: 江蘇頻遭水患，由太湖水洩不暢。

translations.literal: Jiangsu frequently suffered floods because Tai Lake's outflow was obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu suffered frequent flooding because the outflow from Tai Lake was obstructed.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「太湖尾閭在吳淞江及劉河、白茆河，而以吳淞江為最要。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Tai Lake's outlets are the Wusong River and the Liu and Baimao rivers, and the Wusong River is the most important.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Tai Lake drains through the Wusong River and the Liu and Baimao rivers, of which the Wusong is the most important.

sentences.zh: 治吳淞以通海口為最要。

translations.literal: Managing the Wusong to open the sea mouth is the most important."
translations.idiomatic: The essential task is to manage the Wusong so that it opens freely to the sea."

sentences.zh: 」於是以海運節省銀二十餘萬興工，擇賢任事，至八年工竣。

translations.literal: Thereupon using more than two hundred thousand taels saved from sea transport he began work, selecting worthy men for the task; by the eighth year the project was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he launched the project with more than two hundred thousand taels saved from the sea transport reform, selecting capable men to carry it out; by the eighth year the work was completed.

sentences.zh: 又以江以南運道，徒陽運河最易淤阻，而練湖為其上游，孟瀆為其旁支。

translations.literal: Also, south of the Yangzi for the transport route, the Tuyang Canal was most easily silted and blocked, while Lian Lake was its upper reach and Mengdu its branch channel.
translations.idiomatic: He also found that south of the Yangzi the Tuyang Canal on the transport route was most prone to silting, with Lian Lake as its upper reach and the Mengdu channel as a branch.

sentences.zh: 澍自巡漕時，條奏利害，至是先濬徒陽河，將以次舉劉河、白茆、練湖、孟瀆諸工。

translations.literal: Shu since patrolling grain transport had submitted in detail on advantages and harms; at this time he first dredged the Tuyang River, intending in succession to undertake works on the Liu and Baimao rivers, Lian Lake, and Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had laid out the advantages and disadvantages in detail while inspecting grain transport; now he first dredged the Tuyang River, planning in turn to undertake works on the Liu and Baimao rivers, Lian Lake, and the Mengdu channel.

sentences.zh: 後在總督任，與巡撫林則徐合力悉加疏濬，吳中稱為數十年之利，語詳則徐傳。

translations.literal: Later as governor-general, together with Governor Lin Zexu he combined efforts to dredge them all thoroughly; Wu region called it a benefit of several decades—the details are in Lin Zexu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as governor-general, he and the governor Lin Zexu worked together to dredge them all thoroughly; the people of the Wu region called it a benefit not seen in decades—the details are given in Lin Zexu's biography.

sentences.zh: 十年，以捕獲戶部私造假照要犯，加太子少保銜，署兩江總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, for capturing a major criminal who forged Ministry of Revenue credentials, he was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent rank, acted as governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and soon received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, for capturing a major criminal who had forged Ministry of Revenue credentials, he was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and soon received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 時淮鹽敗壞，商困課絀，岌岌不可終日。

translations.literal: At that time Huai salt administration was ruined, merchants were distressed and tax revenue deficient, perilously unable to last another day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Huai salt administration was in ruins, merchants were in distress and tax revenues in deficit, and the system seemed on the verge of collapse.

sentences.zh: 澍疏陳積弊，請大刪浮費，以為補救。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized accumulated abuses and requested large cuts in superfluous expenses as remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized on the accumulated abuses and petitioned for drastic cuts in superfluous expenses as a remedy.

sentences.zh: 議者多主改法課歸場灶，命尚書王鼎、侍郎寶興赴江南查議。

translations.literal: Many in deliberation favored changing the law to assign tax collection to salt fields and furnaces; the emperor ordered Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing to go to Jiangnan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Many deliberators favored changing the law to assign tax collection directly to the salt fields and furnaces; the emperor ordered the minister Wang Ding and the vice minister Bao Xing to go to Jiangnan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 澍謂除弊即以興利，無事輕改舊制，偕鼎等合疏臚陳利害，條上十五事。

translations.literal: Shu said eliminating abuses was itself creating profit; there was no need lightly to change the old system; together with Ding and others he jointly memorialized in detail on advantages and harms, submitting fifteen items.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued that eliminating abuses was itself a way to increase revenue and that there was no need to alter the old system lightly; together with Ding and others he submitted a detailed joint memorial setting forth fifteen proposals.

sentences.zh: 鼎等復請裁鹽政歸總督管理，報可。

translations.literal: Ding and others again requested abolishing the salt commissioner and returning management to the governor-general; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and others further petitioned to abolish the salt commissioner and place management under the governor-general; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 澍受事，繳還鹽政養廉五千兩，裁減衙門陋規十六萬兩有奇，凡淮南之窩價，淮北之壩槓，兩淮之岸費，分別減除，歲計數百萬兩，分設內外二庫，正款貯內庫，雜項貯外庫，杜絕挪墊。

translations.literal: Shu took charge, returned five thousand taels of the salt commissioner's integrity stipend, cut yamen corrupt customs by more than one hundred sixty thousand taels—all Huainan nest prices, Huaibei dam fees, and Two Hu bank charges were reduced respectively, totaling several million taels yearly; he established inner and outer treasuries, regular funds in the inner, miscellaneous in the outer, cutting off diversion.
translations.idiomatic: Shu took charge, returned the salt commissioner's five-thousand-tael integrity stipend, and cut yamen corrupt fees by more than one hundred sixty thousand taels; nest prices in Huainan, dam fees in Huaibei, and bank charges in the Two Hu were all reduced, saving several million taels a year; he established separate inner and outer treasuries, with regular funds in the inner treasury and miscellaneous items in the outer, thereby stopping diversions.

sentences.zh: 革總商以除把持，散輪規以免淹滯，禁糧船回空帶蘆鹽，及商船借官行私，令行禁止，弊肅風清。

translations.literal: He abolished chief merchants to remove monopolistic control, scattered-lot rules to avoid stagnation, forbade grain ships returning empty to carry reed salt and merchant ships using official status for private trade—all strictly prohibited, abuses cleared and customs purified.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the chief merchants to break their monopolistic grip, adopted open-lot rules to prevent stagnation, forbade grain ships returning empty to carry smuggled reed salt and merchant ships using official cover for private trade—all were strictly prohibited, and abuses were swept away.

sentences.zh: 淮北尤疲累，先借款官督商運，繼仿山東、浙江票引兼行之法，於海州所屬中正、板浦、臨興三場擇要隘設局給票，註明斤數運地，無票越境以私論。

translations.literal: Huaibei was especially exhausted; first he borrowed funds for government-supervised merchant transport, then imitated Shandong and Zhejiang methods of combining ticket and quota systems, at Zhongzheng, Banpu, and Linxing salt fields under Haizhou choosing strategic passes to establish bureaus issuing tickets noting weight and destination—without tickets, crossing borders was treated as smuggling.
translations.idiomatic: Huaibei was especially exhausted; he first borrowed government funds to supervise merchant transport, then adopted the Shandong and Zhejiang method of combining ticket and quota systems, establishing bureaus at strategic passes in the Zhongzheng, Banpu, and Linxing salt fields under Haizhou to issue tickets noting weight and destination—anyone crossing borders without a ticket was treated as a smuggler.

sentences.zh: 仍留暢銷之岸，江運八州縣、湖運十一州縣，歸商運。

translations.literal: He still retained banks with brisk sales; eight counties and prefectures by river transport and eleven by lake transport were returned to merchant transport.
translations.idiomatic: He retained the banks with brisk sales, and returned eight counties and prefectures on the river route and eleven on the lake route to merchant transport.

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏准開辦，越半歲，溢銷逾額，复推廣於江運、湖運各岸，減價裁費，商販爭趨，而窩商蠹吏、壩夫岸胥一旦盡失其中飽需索之利，群議沸騰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year memorial approval was granted to begin; within half a year sales exceeded quotas; he further extended to river and lake transport banks, reduced prices and cut fees—merchants rushed in, while nest merchants, corrupt clerks, dam workers, and bank runners suddenly lost all their squeeze profits; public debate boiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the memorial was approved and the system launched; within half a year sales exceeded quotas; he extended the scheme to the river and lake transport banks, cut prices and fees, and merchants flocked to it—while nest merchants, corrupt clerks, dam workers, and bank runners suddenly lost all their illicit profits, and public controversy erupted.

sentences.zh: 言官摭浮言，屢事彈劾，賴宣宗鑑其忠誠，倚畀愈專。

translations.literal: Censorial officials seized on rumors and repeatedly impeached him; relying on the Xuanzong Emperor discerning his loyalty, trust in him grew ever more exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials seized on rumors and repeatedly impeached him; the Daoguang Emperor, recognizing his loyalty, relied on him ever more exclusively.

sentences.zh: 屢請復鹽政專職，皆不許，澍益感奮，力排眾議，毅然持之，卒獲成效。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested restoration of the salt commissioner specialty—all denied; Shu grew more inspired, forcefully rejected public debate, resolutely held to it, and finally achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to restore the separate salt commissioner—all were denied; Shu grew only more determined, forcefully rejected opposition, held firmly to his course, and finally achieved results.

sentences.zh: 道光元年至十年，淮南行六綱，淮北僅行三綱。

translations.literal: From the first to tenth year of Daoguang, Huainan completed six quota cycles, Huaibei only three.
translations.idiomatic: From the first to the tenth year of Daoguang, Huainan completed six quota cycles while Huaibei completed only three.

sentences.zh: 澍承極弊之後，自十一年至十七年，淮南已完六綱有餘，淮北率一歲行兩綱之鹽，盡完從前滯欠，且割淮南懸引，兩淮共完正雜銀二千六百四十餘萬兩，庫貯實存三百餘萬兩。

translations.literal: Shu after extreme abuses—from the eleventh to seventeenth year Huainan completed six cycles with surplus, Huaibei on average moved two cycles' salt per year, clearing all previous arrears, and also applied Huainan's suspended quotas; the Two Hu together completed regular and miscellaneous silver of more than 26.4 million taels, with actual treasury storage of more than three million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Taking charge after the system had reached its lowest point, from the eleventh to the seventeenth year Shu saw Huainan complete six full quota cycles with a surplus, while Huaibei on average moved two cycles' worth of salt a year, clearing all previous arrears and applying Huainan's suspended quotas; the Two Hu together collected more than 26.4 million taels in regular and miscellaneous revenues, with more than three million taels actually in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 兩屆京察，並被褒獎優敘。

translations.literal: In two rounds of capital evaluation he was both praised and given preferential promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In two rounds of the capital evaluation he received both praise and preferential promotion.

sentences.zh: 晚年將推淮北之法於淮南，已病風痺，未竟其施，然天下皆知票鹽減價敵私，為正本清源之計。

translations.literal: In his later years he was about to extend Huaibei methods to Huainan but was already ill with wind paralysis and did not complete the implementation; yet all under heaven knew ticket salt with reduced prices countered smuggling as a plan to rectify the root and purify the source.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he planned to extend the Huaibei methods to Huainan, but was already stricken with paralysis and could not complete the work; yet everyone knew that ticket salt at reduced prices was meant to counter smuggling—a plan to attack the problem at its root.

sentences.zh: 後咸豐中乃卒行之。

translations.literal: Later in the Xianfeng reign it was finally carried out.
translations.idiomatic: It was finally implemented in full during the Xianfeng reign.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，優詔軫惜，稱其「實心任事，不避嫌怨」，晉贈太子太保，依尚書例賜卹，賜其子桄主事，諡文毅。

translations.literal: His death memorial was submitted; an edict graciously mourned him, praising him as "sincere in service, not avoiding resentment," promoted posthumously to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted condolence per minister precedent, gave his son Guang a principal clerk post, posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: When his death memorial reached the throne, an edict mourned him warmly, praising him as "sincere in office and unafraid of resentment," posthumously promoting him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granting funeral honors according to the precedent for ministers, appointing his son Guang as a principal clerk, and giving him the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 祝名宦祠，於海州建專祠。

translations.literal: Enshrined in the shrine of eminent officials; a dedicated shrine was built at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the shrine of eminent officials, and a dedicated shrine was built for him at Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 澍見義勇為，胸無城府。

translations.literal: Shu acted boldly when he saw righteousness and had no hidden schemes in his breast.
translations.idiomatic: Shu acted boldly whenever he saw a righteous cause and harbored no hidden agendas.

sentences.zh: 用人能盡其長，所拔取多至方面節鉞有名。

translations.literal: In employing men he could use their strengths fully; those he promoted mostly rose to famous provincial commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In employing men he brought their strengths fully into play; many of those he promoted rose to become famous provincial governors and commanders.

sentences.zh: 在江南治河、治漕、治鹽，並賴王鳳生、俞德源、姚瑩、黃冕諸人之力。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan governing rivers, grain transport, and salt—all relied on the efforts of Wang Fengsheng, Yu Deyuan, Yao Ying, Huang Mian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan his work on rivers, grain transport, and salt all depended on the efforts of Wang Fengsheng, Yu Deyuan, Yao Ying, Huang Mian, and others.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠、胡林翼皆識之未遇，結為婚姻，後俱為名臣。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang and Hu Linyi both knew him before he had risen to prominence and formed marriage ties; later both became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang and Hu Linyi both knew him before he had risen to prominence, and marriage ties were formed between their families; both later became famous statesmen.

sentences.zh: 所著奏議、詩文集、蜀輶日記、陶桓公年譜、​​陶淵明詩輯註並行世。

translations.literal: His writings—memorials, poetry and prose collections, Sichuan travel diary, chronological biography of Duke Huan of Tao, and collected annotations on Tao Yuanming's poetry—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings—including memorials, collected poetry and prose, a Sichuan travel diary, a chronological biography of Duke Huan of Tao, and collected annotations on Tao Yuanming's poetry—have all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：趙慎畛學有本源，察吏治民，嚴而能恕，所至政無不舉。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Zhao Shenzhen's learning had deep roots; in inspecting officials and governing people he was strict yet forgiving; wherever he went government affairs were invariably accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Zhao Shenzhen's learning had deep roots; in inspecting officials and governing the people he was strict yet forgiving, and wherever he served every undertaking was brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 盧坤治回疆軍需，平湖南瑤，馭廣東夷商，皆有殊績。

translations.literal: Lu Kun in managing western regions military supplies, pacifying Hunan Yao, and controlling Guangdong foreign merchants all had exceptional achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kun's management of military supplies in the western regions, pacification of the Hunan Yao, and handling of foreign merchants in Guangdong were all marked by exceptional achievement.

sentences.zh: 陶澍治水利、漕運、鹽政，垂百年之利，為屏為翰，庶無媿焉。

translations.literal: Tao Shu in governing water conservancy, grain transport, and salt administration left benefits lasting a hundred years; as screen and pillar, he may be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shu's work on water conservancy, grain transport, and the salt monopoly left benefits that would last a century; as a shield and a pillar of the state, he had little to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 道光中年後，海內多事，諸臣並已徂謝，遂無以紓朝廷南顧之憂。

translations.literal: After the middle years of Daoguang, troubles multiplied within the seas; these ministers had all passed away, and there was no one to ease the court's anxious gaze southward.
translations.idiomatic: After the middle years of the Daoguang reign troubles multiplied across the empire; these ministers had all passed away, and there was no one left to ease the court's anxious concern for the south.

sentences.zh: 人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁，其信然哉！

translations.literal: When men pass away like clouds, the state is stricken to exhaustion—how true this is!
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men depart like clouds dispersing, the state is brought to ruin—how true that saying is!
